title: Your First Part: a Gauge Block
summary: Sketch a rectangle, dimension it, and extrude it into a 40 × 20 × 10 mm block. You'll learn the full Onshape → STL → grade workflow.

title: M5 Bolt Spacer
summary: A round spacer that slides over an M5 bolt to hold two robot plates 10 mm apart. Practice circles, concentric constraints, and a through-hole.

spec.label: Center hole
spec.value: Ø5.5 mm (± 0.1): ISO 273 medium clearance for M5

title: Sensor Mounting Plate
summary: A flat plate that bolts a sensor board onto a robot with two M3 screws. Practice symmetric sketches and hole patterns.

spec.label: Holes
spec.value: 2 × Ø3.4 mm (± 0.1): ISO 273 medium clearance for M3

spec.label: Hole spacing
spec.value: 40 mm center-to-center (± 0.15), along the 50 mm side

spec.label: Placement
spec.value: Symmetric about the plate center, on the long centerline

title: NEMA 17 Stepper Motor Mount
summary: Design the plate that holds a NEMA 17 stepper motor, the motor inside most 3D printers. You'll match a real industry-standard bolt pattern.

spec.label: Center bore
spec.value: Ø22.5 mm (± 0.15): clearance for the motor's Ø22 mm boss

spec.label: Bolt pattern
spec.value: 31 × 31 mm square (± 0.15), centered on the bore, edges parallel to the plate

title: Robot Chassis Base Plate (Open Design)
summary: Design the base plate for a small two-wheel robot. The rules below are measured automatically; the AI mentor reviews your layout and your explanation of your design choices.

spec.label: Fastener holes
spec.value: At least 6 round holes between Ø3.0 and Ø5.5 mm (M3 to M5 clearance)

spec.label: Edge margin
spec.value: Every hole or cutout keeps at least 1.5 mm of material to the outer edge

spec.label: Walls between holes
spec.value: At least 1.5 mm of material between any two holes or cutouts

spec.label: Design review
spec.value: 30 points from the AI mentor: motor/caster/battery layout, balance, weight-saving, explanation

designRubric:
Award up to 30 points for design judgment, using only what the screenshots, the measurements and the student's explanation actually show:
- 10: Layout makes sense for a two-wheel differential-drive robot: two motor mounts placed symmetrically   on a common axis, a caster/skid point, and space for a battery and microcontroller.
- 8: Balance and structure: mass roughly centered between wheels and caster, no long thin unsupported   sections, fillets or chamfers where corners would crack or snag.
- 6: Weight-saving or wiring cutouts used sensibly without weakening the plate.
- 6: The written explanation shows design intent (why holes are where they are, which fasteners are used).
If there are no screenshots and no explanation, award at most 6 points and say what was missing.
